e.v: Realistic Crop Rotation stores the four previous crop or fallow entries for each owned field. Use Agronomy to inspect a field, Planning to prepare a repeating cycle, and the Diseases map to monitor risk, outbreaks and treatment coverage.

Select an owned field to review the current crop, up to four previous entries, agronomic advice, nitrogen, pH, treatment coverage and current field status. The weather header helps you choose when to spray.

Select a slot from N+1 to N+4, then choose the main crop and an optional cover crop. Fill consecutive slots: the completed prefix becomes a repeating two-, three- or four-year cycle, including the return from its last slot to its first.

Rotation quality rewards crop and family diversity, winter and spring alternation, nitrogen-producing crops or cover crops, and a legume followed by a cereal. Repeated families or shared diseases returning too soon lower the score.

A configured legume returns nitrogen only when it is destroyed by tillage, not when it is merely harvested. The return is split between the next two crops; with Precision Farming it is written to the nitrogen map, otherwise one fertilizer level is added.

Disease Risk shows the highest current pathogen pressure for the crop growing on each owned field as low, moderate or high. Weather can further change the infection chance, so use this map and the Agronomy weather header together.

An infection starts hidden and appears here only once it begins destroying crop. The map identifies the outbreak among the nine configured diseases; the field card, on-foot HUD and notification then show it too.

Spray early. Fungicide lowers outbreak chance and slows an active disease in proportion to field coverage. Fungicide and nematicide protect sprayed cells from destruction, but cannot restore lost crop or remove disease from the field.

The Treatments map shows ground protected by fungicide or nematicide. Fungicide protection ends on harvested or mown ground. Nematicide protection lasts three months per field and another application renews that duration.

While standing in a field, the HUD adds the two previous crops, visible diseases and active treatments. It also displays numbered growth progress; Precision Farming keeps its own soil, pH, nitrogen and yield information.
Soil protection lasts 3 months per field; reapplication renews the duration.
Nitrogen and pH values are unavailable. Analyse the soil to unlock precise agronomic advice.
After a cereal, sow a legume to restore nitrogen or a break crop to cut foot diseases, and keep two years between cereals.
After a legume, a cereal makes the most of the nitrogen it leaves behind, and another legume should wait three years.
After an oilseed, leave three years before any oilseed returns, with a cereal then a legume as the ideal succession.
After a root crop, allow four years before roots come back, and follow with a cereal to rebuild structure after the late lifting.
After a vegetable, wait three years before repeating it, with a cereal as a clean break.
After a grass ley, a cereal cashes in the fertility and structure built up under the sward.

High sclerotinia risk: wait at least 3 years before bringing canola, mustard, sunflower, soybean, pea, bean, potato or carrot back; fungicide limits damage on sprayed ground but does not clean the field.
High nematode risk: wait at least 3 years before bringing sugar beet, beetroot, canola, mustard or spinach back; nematicide protects sprayed ground but does not remove nematodes.
Moderate sclerotinia risk: leave more time before bringing canola, mustard, sunflower, soybean, pea, bean, potato or carrot back; rain can raise the risk.
Moderate nematode risk: leave more time before bringing beets, canola, mustard or spinach back.

Use AMISTAR in sprayers to apply a fungicide treatment to at-risk crops.
Use VELUM PRIME in sprayers to apply a nematicide treatment to crops exposed to nematodes.
High phoma risk: wait at least 4 years before bringing canola or mustard back; fungicide limits damage on sprayed ground but does not clean the field.
High take-all risk: break the cereal sequence with oat, a legume or an oilseed; no product protects against this disease, and more time between sensitive cereals lowers future risk.
High septoria risk: rain can raise the risk further, and fungicide limits damage on sprayed ground.
High rust risk: mild damp weather can raise the risk further, and fungicide limits damage on sprayed ground.
High fusarium risk: avoid wheat directly after maize and consecutive cereals; fungicide limits damage on sprayed ground, and rain can accelerate the disease.
High late blight risk: cool damp weather can raise the risk further, and fungicide limits damage on sprayed ground.
High clubroot risk: wait as long as possible before bringing canola or mustard back; no product protects against this disease, which can remain in the field indefinitely.
Moderate phoma risk: leave more time before bringing canola or mustard back.
Moderate take-all risk: avoid a third cereal in a row.
Moderate septoria risk: rain can raise the risk further.
Moderate rust risk: mild damp weather can raise the risk further.
Moderate fusarium risk: leave more time between cereals and maize.
Moderate late blight risk: cool damp weather can raise the risk further.
Moderate clubroot risk: leave more time before bringing canola or mustard back.
